q: We live abroad, away from my family, so support options are limited. My husband’s mother offered to come stay with us for up to three months after the birth to help, and I know it comes from love and good intentions.
cx: At almost 13 weeks, recently bereaved of her own mother, weighing a three-month helper stay.

q: Part of me desperately wants support. Another part of me wants silence, privacy, and space to fall apart safely.
cx: Her conflict over help after the birth.

q: I have cleaned everything I am able, I have stayed on top of the trash, dishes, air filter, and cat boxes. I scrubbed the sinks, toilets, floors, fridge, trash cans, and seal up the cats food. I have had plumbers come out to clean and treat all the drains, I have cleaned the oven and then, at her request, removed the stove from the house.
cx: His wife at 9 weeks gags the moment she enters their home.

q: She misses me, the cats, our home. Its just not home without her there. We really don't have money to move as I'm the only one working.
cx: She is staying elsewhere because of the smell.

q: I told him I don’t know if it will be a good idea because we try to save our PTOs for the baby and take a few days off and drive there will be very hard on my body. I looked at the flight tickets, it is around $400 person, my boyfriend think it is very expensive to fly to his hometown and he insists to drive there.
cx: At 20 weeks, her boyfriend's mother plans a shower ten hours away for around 30 weeks; she is from another country.

q: my boyfriend thinks since I am just sitting in the car, I should not feel tired at all. I told him even now, sitting in the car for more than 2 hours is killing my back and my hip. I also think spending $700 is a lot which I can use for the baby.
TLDR: my MIL is staying with us for 3 weeks to “help” but I feel like she’s taking on the mother role of my newborn and I’m a guest in my own house.
cx: One week into a three-week helper stay after a hard start.

q: Like I picked him up and she told me to go rest and took him from my arms.
cx: What the help looks like day to day.

q: Like I’ll start vacuuming and she’ll offer to take baby upstairs instead of offer to finish vacuuming.
cx: Help with the baby instead of the house.

q: MIL said some family should save their pto for September to they can fly in and meet baby.
cx: First baby due in September; nine in-laws already asking when they can visit.

q: I think I will just play it by ear and see how recovery goes. I want my parents to meet baby first and then they can meet her. Just want to ensure anyone coming over early on will also help support us and not just meet baby

My husband and I both agreed several months ago that my mom would come when the baby was due to be here, help with the house/dogs, and keep me preoccupied and his mom would come later maybe a few days after the baby was born.
cx: At 40 weeks, families live 6 and 10+ hours away; the staggered plan made months earlier.

q: this afternoon my husband gets a random call from his mom letting us know that she is in the car and on the way to come see us and she’ll be here in a few hours.
cx: Her mother-in-law arrives unannounced while she waits past her due date.

q: My mom got a two bed Airbnb nearby and we had told her she could stay there a few months ago when it was booked.
cx: Lodging booked months ahead for the helper visit.
